text: Hunger is the best sauce in the world.
Remember, a stitch in time saves nine.
There's no such thing as a free lunch.
You have to spend money to make money.
He who is afraid of asking is ashamed of learning.
It's best to let sleeping dogs lie.
Blood is always thicker than water.
Laughter is the best medicine.
Always save something for a rainy day.
Rain at seven, fine at eleven.
Even a cat may look at a king.
You can't run with the hare and hunt with the hounds.
Never set a fox to guard the henhouse.
Do not talk with your mouth full.
You're only as old as you feel.
Repetition is the mother of learning.
Learning is a treasure that follows its owner everywhere.
The best defense is a good offense.
Win without boasting, lose without excuses.
Always keep your eye on the ball.
The longest way round is the shortest way home.
The tallest trees catch the most wind.
A year of snow, a year of plenty.
If February gives much snow, a fine summer it doth bestow.
A dry March and a wet May fill barns and bays with corn and hay.
Ring around the moon means rain soon.
No weather is ill if the wind be still.
When the wind is in the west, the weather is at its best.
You should never buy a pig in a poke.
If wishes were horses, beggars would ride.
Two dogs fight for a bone, and a third runs away with it.
While the grass grows, the horse starves.
A bird is known by its note, and a man by his talk.
When the fox preaches, look to your geese.
Every Jack must have his Jill.
When poverty comes in at the door, love flies out of the window.
Never marry for money; you can borrow it cheaper.
Good company on the road is the shortest cut.
Lend your money and lose your friend.
Fresh air impoverishes the doctor.
The road to a friend's house is never long.
Many a good cow has a bad calf.
Children are poor men's riches.
Better a little fire to warm us than a big one to burn us.
A place for everything, and everything in its place.
What can't be cured must be endured.
One rotten apple spoils the whole barrel.
Bread never falls but on its buttered side.
Good health is better than great wealth.
Sickness comes on horseback but departs on foot.
It's bad luck to walk under a ladder.
Fear makes the wolf bigger than he is.
You never know what you can do till you try.
Grasp the nettle, and it will not sting.
Patience is a plaster for all sores.
The mill cannot grind with the water that is past.
One of these days is none of these days.
Everything has an end, and a sausage has two.
Great minds think alike, but fools seldom differ.
It's out of the frying pan and into the fire.
Don't throw the baby out with the bathwater.
It's no use locking the stable door after the horse has bolted.
The shoemaker's children go barefoot.
Don't cut off your nose to spite your face.
Give him an inch and he'll take a mile.
In for a penny, in for a pound.
A new broom sweeps clean, but the old one knows the corners.
Money is round and rolls away.
Every man knows where his own shoe pinches.
The nail that sticks out gets hammered down.
The best time to plant a tree was twenty years ago; the second best time is now.
Dig the well before you are thirsty.
If you want to go fast, go alone; if you want to go far, go together.
Speak of the devil and he is sure to appear.
Better an open enemy than a false friend.
It is a poor heart that never rejoices.
No bees, no honey; no work, no money.
If you chase two rabbits, you will catch neither.
Two boys are half a boy, and three boys are no boy at all.
There is no garden without its weeds.
